choices.reason: p-Methylbenzyl alcohol measured 5.2/8.1 mL at 0/1 but 39.4/66.4 mL at 10/1. This matched-loading 5/1 point locates the sharp ratio response that the prior 10/1 prediction missed.

Naphthylmethanol measured 6.1/11.9 mL at 0/1, with V2 much earlier than predicted. The 10/1 prediction of 28.5/49.9 mL tests transfer of the benzyl-alcohol ratio response to a larger aromatic group; evidence for transfer is weak.
Dibenzylamine measured 22.1/37.2 mL at 5/1, later than predicted. Its 10/1 prediction of 42.9/74.5 mL tests whether the model captures the next PE-rich step for this amine.
Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde measured 6.9/23.0 mL at 5/1 and 23.5/56.0 mL at 20/1. The 50/1 prediction of 33.3/75.1 mL tests whether its V2 continues rising as strongly as observed.

Methoxy aromatics showed opposite prediction errors at low and high PE ratios. This 50/1 methoxybenzaldehyde prediction of 26.6/48.4 mL probes whether the high-ratio error transfers to another carbonyl-containing methoxy aromatic; evidence is weak.
Nitroacetophenone measured 25.6/55.1 mL at 10/1 after early elution at 0/1. The matched-loading 20/1 prediction of 40.3/85.9 mL tests the continued rise in V2 and elution width.

Several methylbenzonitriles eluted earlier than predicted at PE-rich ratios. This 50/1 fluorobenzonitrile prediction of 14.8/33.3 mL tests whether that error transfers to a different nitrile substituent; the chemical inference is weak.

The benzyl-substituted β-ketoester measured 57.0/97.5 mL at 50/1 and 50 µL, much later than predicted. This 150 µL point at the same ratio probes loading sensitivity of its high V2 and interval width.
This fluorinated aryl ketone is predicted at 14.3/30.9 mL at 20/1. Paired with the 50/1 choice, it tests a solvent-ratio response on one molecule; direct measured support is absent.

At matched loading, the fluorinated aryl ketone prediction rises to 16.5/37.7 mL at 50/1. The pair tests whether the model transfers the ratio effect across the aryl carbonyl family; evidence is weak.
Iodophenol measured 52.8/97.9 mL at 50/1, far above its prior prediction. The 20/1 prediction of 41.3/70.4 mL tests whether that underpredicted PE-rich response is already present at a lower ratio.

Benzyl benzoate measured roughly 16/24–27 mL at 30/1 across 50 and 150 µL loading. This 100/1, 150 µL experiment pairs with pending 100/1, 50 µL data to probe both the high-ratio rise and loading effect.
Ethyl acetoacetate measured V2 of 25.3 mL at 5/1 but 66.9 mL at 20/1, the latter far above prediction. This 10/1 point locates the onset of the wide PE-rich elution interval.
Cyclohexyl acrylate measured only 7.4/17.0 mL at 50/1 versus a much later prior prediction. Its revised 5/1 prediction of 6.7/13.5 mL tests whether it remains early across a large eluent change.

Bromobenzofuran measured 5.0/14.1 mL at 50/1 and 100 µL, far earlier than predicted. The 150 µL candidate at the same ratio tests whether that early result persists with a loading change; its revised prediction is 9.4/19.2 mL.

This tertiary benzylic alcohol is predicted at 21.6/35.1 mL at 20/1. Other aromatic alcohols showed strong ratio dependence, but substitution and conditions differ, so this is a weak structural-transfer probe.

hypotheses.content: The earlier steep-retention prediction for diethyl malonate remains contradicted: measured 5/1, 10/1, 20/1 and 50/1 outcomes all have V1 below 6 mL and V2 below 8 mL. Its phenyl-substituted analogue is much later; that chemical difference matters.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural distinction causes the phenyl-substituted analogue to retain while diethyl malonate stays early?

hypotheses.content: The earlier high-ratio plateau hypothesis for methyl benzoylformate remains contradicted: V2 measured 33.3 mL at 20/1 and 62.0 mL at 50/1 despite near-flat prior predictions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where between 20/1 and 50/1 does V2 rise most sharply?

hypotheses.content: Cyanobenzophenone has a strongly nonlinear measured ratio response: V2 rises from 21.3 mL at 5/1 to 117.9 mL at 50/1. Earlier predictions were too late at 5/1 and 10/1 but too early at 50/1.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which intermediate high-PE ratio captures the curve's steepest section?

hypotheses.content: Nitroacetophenone measured 3.9/11.7 mL at 0/1 and 25.6/55.1 mL at 10/1. The large solvent-ratio response is observed, while its predicted size at 20/1 remains untested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does V2 approach the predicted 85.9 mL at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Ring-nitrogen prediction errors remain structure and ratio dependent. Phenylpyridine was predicted closely at 10/1 and 20/1 but underpredicted at 50/1; methylquinoline was fairly close at 2/1 and 5/1 but strongly underpredicted at 10/1. Dimethylpyridine was overpredicted at 5/1 and 10/1.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which ring-nitrogen structures show abrupt high-ratio increases rather than a smooth shared correction?

hypotheses.content: Two phenols had substantially underpredicted V2 at 50/1, including iodophenol. Phenolic aldehydes at 0/1 instead had V2 overpredictions. This supports a condition- and substitution-specific effect, not a universal phenol rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is iodophenol already later than predicted at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: β-Ketoester responses vary by substitution and PE/EA ratio. Cyclopropyl β-ketoester was predicted closely at 5/1, moderately overpredicted at 10/1, and strongly underpredicted at 20/1. Ethyl acetoacetate V2 was strongly underpredicted at 20/1, and a benzyl-substituted β-ketoester was strongly underpredicted at 50/1.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At matched loadings, where do V2 and its prediction error accelerate between 5/1 and 50/1?

hypotheses.content: Methoxy-aromatic error changes with ratio as well as structure. Trimethoxybenzene was earlier than predicted at 2/1 and 5/1 but later at 50/1. Methoxybenzophenone was earlier than predicted at 5/1 but later at 20/1 and 50/1. The crossover location is unmeasured for both.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does a different methoxy carbonyl compound at 50/1 also elute later than predicted?

hypotheses.content: Aminobenzonitrile was predicted closely at 0/1, too late at 2/1, and much too early at 5/1. The sharp response between 2/1 and 5/1 differs from the early elution of methylbenzonitriles at PE-rich ratios; a general nitrile rule is unsupported.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does fluorobenzonitrile remain early at 50/1, or does its substitution change the response?

hypotheses.content: Iodobenzoate at 50/1 had V1 near 5 mL at both 50 and 150 µL, while V2 increased from 22.6 to 29.3 mL. The broad elution interval and loading effect on V2 are observed, but the cause is uncertain.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Would a matched replicate confirm the V2 loading effect?

hypotheses.content: Oxime V1/V2 rise from 5.8/11.4 mL at 2/1 to 16.4/45.7 mL at 20/1 and 43.1/119.2 mL at 50/1. The 20/1 prediction was far too late, while 50/1 V2 was underpredicted; the predicted ratio curve had the wrong shape.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At which ratio between 20/1 and 50/1 does its elution interval expand most?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic alcohols can show strong ratio dependence, but transfer across structures is untested. p-Methylbenzyl alcohol measured 5.2/8.1 mL at 0/1 and 39.4/66.4 at 10/1; naphthylmethanol measured 6.1/11.9 at 0/1. The 10/1 p-methylbenzyl prediction was much too early.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1, where is p-methylbenzyl alcohol on its steep rise, and does naphthylmethanol respond similarly by 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Dibenzylamine measured 22.1/37.2 mL at 5/1, later than its premeasurement 16.6/27.3 mL prediction. A stronger retention response at 10/1 is plausible but untested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does measured 10/1 V1/V2 approach the 42.9/74.5 mL prediction?

hypotheses.content: Ortho-nitrobenzaldehyde measured 6.9/23.0 mL at 5/1 and 23.5/56.0 mL at 20/1, with the latter later than predicted. Its 50/1 response is not yet observed; comparison with the para isomer is confounded by other conditions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does 50/1 V2 exceed the current 75.1 mL prediction?

hypotheses.content: Benzyl benzoate measured roughly 16/24–27 mL at 30/1 across two loading amounts. The high-ratio 100/1 response and its loading sensitivity remain untested.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How do V1 and V2 at 100/1 compare across 50 and 150 µL loading?

hypotheses.content: Cyclohexyl acrylate measured 7.4/17.0 mL at 50/1, far earlier than its prior 28.3/45.7 mL prediction. After retraining, the 5/1 prediction is early; whether the measured response is nearly flat across ratios is unknown.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 5/1 measurement also remain early?

hypotheses.content: Bromobenzofuran measured 5.0/14.1 mL at 50/1 and 100 µL, much earlier than its prior prediction. A 150 µL measurement at the same ratio can test persistence and loading sensitivity, but one observation is insufficient for a mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does its 50/1 V1 remain near 5 mL at 150 µL?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements sharpened several ratio-dependent errors: p-methylbenzyl alcohol is early at 0/1 but very late at 10/1; oxime and β-ketoester V2 curves change more sharply than predictions; methoxy aromatics change error sign across ratios. I chose intermediate conditions and matched-loading contrasts to locate those changes. The brominated acid returned V2 = -0.1 mL below V1 = 0.13 mL, so I treated that record as an anomalous measurement rather than evidence for an elution mechanism and made no acid-based selection.
